skill.name: researching-with-deepwiki
skill.description: Research GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket repositories with the DeepWiki MCP server. Use it to explore unfamiliar codebases, architecture, feature implementation, and contribution workflows.
skill.summary: Use DeepWiki MCP to research remote repositories and understand codebase architecture.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static external command findings are Markdown fences, inline repository examples, or a manual verification command, so they are false positives. The confirmed risk is intended network use of DeepWiki and Devin.ai MCP endpoints, especially when private repository context is involved. No prompt injection, malicious command execution, or hardcoded real secret was found.

remediation.suggestion: Add a clear notice that repository URLs, prompts, and private repository context may be sent to DeepWiki or Devin.ai.
Require users to confirm they have authorization before using the Devin.ai endpoint for private repositories.
Tell users not to commit bearer tokens and to store private endpoint credentials in approved local settings or secret storage.

content.value_statement: Unfamiliar repositories are slow to understand from files alone. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to query DeepWiki for architecture, feature, and contribution research.
actual_capabilities: Guides setup of the public DeepWiki MCP endpoint for repository research.
Shows private repository configuration through the Devin.ai DeepWiki endpoint.
Provides prompts for architecture, directory, feature, and contribution analysis.
Supports comparisons between implementations across public repositories.
Explains when to use DeepWiki instead of local file search tools.
Includes a local verification script for checking DeepWiki MCP configuration.
limitations: Requires external MCP network access to DeepWiki or Devin.ai.
Private repositories require valid credentials and proper authorization.
Cached analysis may not reflect the latest repository commits.
Not intended for local workspace files or library API documentation.

use_cases.title: Understand a New Repository
use_cases.description: Map the architecture, modules, and important flows before changing unfamiliar code.

use_cases.title: Plan Open Source Contributions
use_cases.description: Research contribution workflow, tests, labels, and implementation patterns before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Compare Technical Approaches
use_cases.description: Study how multiple projects solve similar problems before choosing an implementation strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a Public Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use DeepWiki to analyze github.com/owner/repo. Summarize the main architecture, core modules, and where a new contributor should start.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use DeepWiki to explain how feature name is implemented in github.com/owner/repo. Include key files, data flow, and important tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Projects
prompt_templates.prompt: Use DeepWiki to compare how github.com/org/first and github.com/org/second handle the same technical concern. Highlight design differences and risks.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Contribution Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use DeepWiki to research github.com/owner/repo for a planned change. Identify relevant modules, tests, contribution workflow, and review risks.

output_examples.input: Analyze the architecture of a public web framework repository.
output_examples.output: A concise architecture map with major modules, request flow, extension points, and recommended files for deeper review.

output_examples.input: Find how authentication is handled in a repository.
output_examples.output: A feature walkthrough that names the likely components, explains control flow, and notes tests or examples to inspect.

output_examples.input: Compare cache invalidation across two libraries.
output_examples.output: A comparison of strategies, tradeoffs, project-specific terminology, and questions to verify against source code.

best_practices: Ask focused questions that name a repository, feature, or path.
Confirm private repository authorization before using authenticated DeepWiki endpoints.
Verify DeepWiki findings against source files before making code changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use DeepWiki for local workspace files when local search tools are available.
Do not paste credentials, secrets, or sensitive snippets into repository research prompts.
Do not rely on cached answers for current release behavior without verification.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code research remote repositories through DeepWiki MCP.

faq.question: Does it work with private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, when users configure the Devin.ai DeepWiki endpoint and have proper repository authorization.

faq.question: Does it replace local file search?
faq.answer: No. Use local search tools for files in the current workspace.

faq.question: Is it for library API documentation?
faq.answer: No. It is for repository research, architecture review, and implementation investigation.

faq.question: What data may leave my environment?
faq.answer: Repository URLs, prompts, and private repository context may be sent to DeepWiki or Devin.ai.

faq.question: How can I verify setup?
faq.answer: Run the included verification script to check whether DeepWiki MCP appears in Claude settings.
